items.title: Wi-Fi 8 is upon us, so here are two routers we saw at Computex that should be hitting the shops soon
items.summary: Unsurprisingly, Asus ROG is launching its Wi-Fi 8 routers with an extreme gaming monster.
items.body: Last week at IFA 2026 TP-Link announced two new Wi-Fi 8 routers —the Archer 9 Ultra and the Deco 8 Ultra—though the actual price and release date aren’t yet known, other than availability being later this year. While TP-Link claimed these are the first Wi-Fi 8 routers to be revealed, this isn't quite the case: Asus showed off its Wi-Fi 8 ROG Rapture GT-BN98 at Computex in June, and we were there having a proper gawk. This is a premium gaming router that’s loaded up with features and game optimisations, and with classic completely-OTT ROG looks. Asus also showed its more mainstream ZenWiFi BN12 at Computex for normal people. Pricing and availability have not yet been announced—though review samples of the ROG Rapture GT-BN98 are expected to be available very soon, so it’s not far off. Wi-Fi 8 isn’t so much about boosting speed over Wi-Fi 7: stability under heavy load is the main objective of the new standard, as we continue to saturate the Wi-Fi airwaves with ever more demanding uses. items.title: Corporations want to kill physical media because it suits them, but Big Box PC game packaging just got a second chance
items.summary: It's now much easier to take the DIY approach.
items.body: If you were alive and sentient in the nineties you probably harbour some fondness for the "big box" PC games of yore. Back then, rather than buy an ephemeral digital license for a game, you'd head to a store to buy a huge box bedecked in lavish art, inside which you'd find a handful of 3.5-inch floppy discs or a CD-ROM, usually a substantial glossy manual, and if you were lucky, maybe even some extras like stickers or drink coasters. There's been renewed interest in the ye olde big box PC game, especially in the wake of Sony's announcement it will discontinue physical PlayStation games. Some proactive folk have gone viral for manufacturing their own physical Steam games . Now GOG has offered its own alternative: printable big boxes based on scans of real commercial packages from the golden era of game packaging. In collaboration with Big Box Collection—which is a fan-operated trove of big box 3D scans—GOG is now offering those 3D scans with five entries in its GOG Preservation Program. items.title: Thousand Hells is a 'tactical narrative' feast of infernal storytelling, but its defeats can feel brutal
items.summary: From the developer of King of Dragon Pass, a gorgeously imagined meat grinder for hapless adventuring parties.
items.body: In Thousand Hells: The Underworld heists, I've sort of taken on the role of the dad in that one tweet about feeding cats to coyotes. But rather than serving up pets to jackals, I'm dutifully feeding bands of doomed adventurers into the psychological, corporeal, and spiritual wood chipper of the "tactical narrative" game's bespoke hellscapes. Those hellscapes—from the primordial twilight taigas of the Midnight North, to the melting fever-dream dominion of the Hell of Nightmares—form a mesmerizing kaleidoscope of abyssal imagination. Made by the developer behind the phenomenal King of Dragon Pass and Six Ages games , its pedigree is obvious as each game guides my hand-picked party of hell raiders through encounters rich with the implied culture, tradition, and history of their respective afterlives. I just wish I weren't spending quite as much time feeling like my efforts are futile. items.title: Breaking Benjamin frontman pauses concert to rant about Fallout 4 modding beef: 'There was a modder in the community that was really mean to me'
items.summary: The singer and guitarist spent several minutes asking fans to download his Fallout 4 'True First Person' mod after another modder criticized it.
items.body: Local Man Benjamin Burnley interrupts a Breaking Benjamin concert with a rant about his True First Person 1.2 Fallout 4 mod from r/Fallout An amazing scene played out over the weekend at a Breaking Benjamin concert in Holmdel, NJ, as captured by Reddit user im_all_ears (embedded above). Band frontman Benjamin Burnley spent over four minutes imploring the audience to download his Fallout 4 mod in an effort to stick it to another modder who Burnley says bullied him over the quality of his work. "There was a modder in the community that was really mean to me and bullying me, saying, 'Oh, your mod is shit. You don't know what you're fucking doing,'" said Burnley. "So I'm doing this every fucking night, and blowing his fucking downloads out of the water." That was a mere two minutes into the four-and-a-half minute rant. items.title: مورينيو ينقذ فينيسيوس من جحيم البرنابيو بخطوة مفاجئة
items.summary: رسالة من المدرب للجميع
items.body: رسالة من المدرب للجميع قام البرتغالي جوزيه مورينيو، مدرب ريال مدريد، بلفتة مميزة مع نجم الفريق، البرازيلي فينيسيوس جونيور، خلال مباراة إنتر ميلان. واستهل ريال مدريد، مشواره في دوري أبطال أوروبا، بفوز مثير على ضيفه إنتر ميلان، بهدفين لهدف، في اللقاء الذي جمعهما اليوم الثلاثاء، بملعب سانتياجو برنابيو. وفي الدقيقة 87، وبعد هدف الفريق الإيطالي، قرر جوزيه مورينيو استبدال فينيسيوس جونيور، الذي تعرض لصيحات استهجان خلال الشوط الثاني.  كان البرازيلي نشيطًا للغاية طوال المباراة، رغم خروجه دون أن يُسهم في تسجيل أي هدف. ووفقا لصحيفة " آس "، فإنه أثناء استبدال فينيسيوس بكاريراس، سُمعت صافرات عديدة في ملعب سانتياجو برنابيو، موجهة إلى المهاجم البرازيلي. يمكنكم مناقشة الموضوعات والأخبار بشكل أعمق في منتديات "كووورة"  وهنا بدأت اللقطة المميزة.. رد فينيسيوس بالتصفيق، ناظرًا نحو المدرجات، بينما فعل جوزيه مورينيو الشيء نفسه، رافضًا إبعاد نظره. رافق المدرب البرتغالي اللاعب البرازيلي في طريقه إلى مقاعد البدلاء، وصفق له طوال الوقت. وعندما التفت فينيسيوس ليرد على بعض المشجعين، عانقه مورينيو بحرارة وربت على ظهره عدة مرات.. تُظهر هذه اللفتة بوضوح العلاقة الودية بينهما، كما أنها بمثابة دعم علني من المدرب للاعبه.

items.summary: Setting the stage to perfection.
items.body: The reception to Final Fantasy 14: Dawntrail's story has been as much of a journey as the expansion itself. It was never going to be easy, being the first expansion to build a brand-new arc following a decade of excellent storytelling, and unfortunately it didn't quite land initially. Criticisms around its core narrative have largely abated over the last few patches, though, as we near the next expansion Evercold in January. And with its final batch of quests now unleashed upon players I'm here to declare: this might be the greatest final MSQ patch we've ever received. Spoilers ahead for Patch 7.56 of Dawntrail, if that wasn't already obvious. Dawntrail's final quests serve as less of a light teaser for what's to come in Evercold, and instead feel like a straight-up prologue to the expansion. That's wildly different from what I've come to expect from these patch quests. Sure, we usually spend a few patches building up to what's next, dropping little hints and then using the final patch quests to introduce a new character or setting as a fun little hype-builder. items.summary: It's got an entry-level MSRP, but still feels like an enthusiast-level device.
items.body: Razer had a bountiful display of products to show at Gamescom 2026, many of which come with substantial price tags. However, my eyes lit up when I saw the new Razer Reclusa X Mini 65% keyboard , especially as it's got a $50/£60 MSRP. I picked it up and twisted it around in my hands, expecting it to bend like a piece of cardboard thanks to some budget materials. Nope, it seems like a very solidly-built device—which is pretty impressive given the affordable price tag. The doubleshot ABS keycaps, in combination with Razer's Gen-3 orange tactile switches , feel downright high-end. It makes a good noise, too, producing the sort of weighty thock I normally associate with much more expensive keebs. items.title: New RTX 5070 variant could help bolster GPU supply but it surely won't help prices
items.summary: Nvidia is reportedly prepping a new version of the RTX 5070 potentially using failed RTX 5070 Ti or RTX 5080 cores.
items.body: There are reports today that Nvidia is going to be releasing a new variant of its GeForce RTX 5070 graphics card with a cut-down GB203 GPU instead of the GB205 chip it originally launched with. Could this be good news for consumers? Well, no and maybe. The idea behind using bigger chips to fill out the inventory of smaller cards basically gives manufacturers something to do with graphics processors that don't have enough functional units to power a bigger card. Here we're talking about the same GPU as that used in the far more powerful RTX 5070 Ti and RTX 5080 graphics cards. The RTX 5070 doesn't currently use the full GB205 die, but its complement of 6144 CUDA cores isn't far off the maximum of 6400 the full chip can offer, so it already has some failsafe headroom built in. Compare that with the GB203 used by the RTX 5080 and that card is using the full silicon package of its chip. That could maybe be seen as quite a gamble on the yields coming from the TSMC 4N process, but it is mature, and Nvidia already has the RTX 5070 Ti, with its 8960 CUDA cores to mop up any GPUs that don't quite fit the full RTX 5080 bill. AI capabilities are starting to serve as national and international litmus tests for soft and hard power, but these capabilities depend on the physical hardware underneath them. items.title: Big chipmakers are already committed to using ASML's next-generation production technology by as soon as 2028
items.summary: High NA EUV and even 12-inch photomasks.
items.body: Samsung is set to use ASML's latest high NA EUV machines for "volume manufacturing" by 2028, and TSMC is set to do the same from 2030, according to the world's sole EUV machine maker (via Bloomberg ). 'High NA EUV' stands for "high numerical aperture extreme ultraviolet", and refers to the tippity top-end chipmaking technology found in ASML's most advanced machines. The technology has been in active use by Intel and SK hynix for a short while . It allows for faster production and higher yields thanks to how it simplifies the chipmaking process, removing some production steps. It also produces more dense wafers. According to Bloomberg, ASML will also be working with Samsung, TSMC, Nvidia, and Apple to move from 6-inch photomasks to 12-inch ones, though I can only see official ASML announcements for the first three . These are the designs the EUV optics shine through to stencil chip designs onto wafers, and upping the mask to 12 inches will mean more of a wafer can be covered with each EUV shot, meaning fewer shots need to be fixed together and, well, performed at all, meaning cheaper and more efficient production. items.summary: Things are still chugging along over there, it seems.
items.body: Despite a cloud of doom and gloom hanging over Riot's mysterious MMO in the wake of 2XKO's closure–including well-founded concerns from our own Harvey Randall —its co-founder seems confident in its ongoing development. At least, that's what I'm parsing from his relative non-answer when pressed about it during a panel at PAX West over the weekend. Marc Merrill dropped a mention of the MMO while answering a different question during the panel, which was immediately chased up by host Greg Miller with half-joking prompts for further morsels of information. Merrill mostly laughs it off, but does give a somewhat half-answer that at least indicates development of it is moving along at… some sort of pace. But I can't help but wonder, quietly, whether or not Final Fantasy has fallen into the same 'fear of new IP trap' as other games. That's not to say that the FF series isn't getting new games. Final Fantasy 16 came out in 2023 and snagged a solid 79 from us in our Final Fantasy 16 review . And yet, a small part of me wonders what new and exciting games we might've gotten if Square Enix had devoted the Remake team to making new final fantasies, rather than spending three entire big-budget titles and over half a decade rehashing a classic. Yet while there have been some good examples in recent years like Skin Deep and New Blood's early access Thief-like Gloomwood , a lot of the experiments in indie imsim design have been simply too janky for me to enjoy. Part of the problem is I'm a highly tactile player, and my primary concern when playing any game is whether it feels good beneath the fingers. If a game falls at that initial hurdle, then it's likely (though not inevitable) that I'll drop it pretty quickly. Fortunately, I had the opposite experience with Deficit , an indie imsim with such a strong sense of physicality that I kept playing the demo despite some clear issues. Developed by Item42, which previously created the cooperative shooter Perish , Deficit sees you play as a freelance spy in a dilapidated, dystopian world. items.summary: Rat's entertainment.
items.body: I was largely nonplussed by Gamescom's Opening Night Live , particularly its relentless barrage of identikit fantasy action games that I struggled to tell apart. But one game stood out like a rat-powered computer in an elven glade, and that was Ontos , Frictional Games' latest horror adventure/existential crisis generator. The Gamescom trailer was a barrage of unsettling, distinctive imagery, from rodent server-racks to slack-jawed dudes with electrodes protruding from their heads. I was instantly intrigued and keen to learn more, so I was delighted to discover that Frictional graced us with a longer look at Ontos in action. The 10-minute showcase focuses on the same part of the game as the shorter trailer. But it adds significant context to how Ontos plays and the kinds of challenges you'll be dealing with. items.title: Civilization 7 will finally enter the atomic age in 2027, via a free update Firaxis says will be 'even bigger in scope' than last year's Test of Time
items.summary: First expansion "Earthrise" also announced.
items.body: Despite more than a year of updates and at least one massive overhaul, Civilization 7 remains as stubbornly divisive as ever. May's enormous Test of Time update brought significant mechanical reworks and a fresh influx of players to Firaxis' latest entry in the 4X series. But with Steam reviews still sitting at ' Mixed' , with 51% positive, it ultimately did little to shift player opinion. This is partly because numerous aspects of Civ 7 are still rudimentary compared to previous games, including the ability to wage nuclear war. While Firaxis' latest allows players to drop atom bombs on their enemies via World War 2 bombers, its final, modern age ends in 1950, meaning many advanced technologies, including nuclear submarines and ICBMs, are not featured in the game. Fortunately, this is going to change. Alongside the release of update 1.5.0 —which adds features like improved resource generation and an Earth map where your faction starts at their historically-accurate location—Firaxis outlined its update plans for Civ 7 over the next year. items.title: Ex-BioWare designer says doom and gloom about the next Mass Effect is overstated: 'I think that they can do it'
items.summary: "I think BioWare can do it if we just leave them alone to do what they do best."
items.body: Given that Anthem and Mass Effect Andromeda were widely considered disappointments, and Dragon Age: The Veilguard had a divisive reception, there's a certain amount of skepticism about the Mass Effect game BioWare is currently working on. Some have even suggested it might not come out at all . Armando Troisi, a cinematic designer on the Mass Effect trilogy and lead cinematic designer on Mass Effect 2, thinks it's all a bit much. "I think BioWare, when they break it down and do that singleplayer, interactive narrative-driven, deep combat, progression-driven game, really, there's nobody that can touch them," Troisi told FRVR . "It's kind of like the [Master] Chief, it's like going on a walkabout and finding themselves and coming back. I think BioWare can do it if we just leave them alone to do what they do best." Troisi said that when he was working at BioWare the studio knew what kind of game it was best at making, and that all they need is to get back to that. "The vision was always clear," he said.
